Container runtime spec written to /ai/prompts/container-runtime.md (666 lines). Recommendation: containerd via CRI gRPC. Rationale: ContainerRuntime trait makes it swappable at any time; 35-50 MB RSS not a constraint at 1 GB node RAM; saves ~2000-4000 lines of OCI implementation work vs direct path. Covers: CRI protocol, all three candidates, comparison table, full integration spec (tonic codegen, pod lifecycle, status polling, resource limits, log collection), ContainerRuntime trait definition, RSS budget, phased delivery. Top risks: proto drift, netns timing.

State store spec written to /ai/prompts/state-store.md (932 lines). Recommendation: SQLite. Rationale: target workload peaks at ~17 writes/second; SQLite WAL handles >1000 writes/s with p99 <10ms — two orders of magnitude headroom. LMDB advantages irrelevant at this scale; lmdb-rkv crate is dormant; MDB_MAP_FULL is operational risk. Covers: K8s storage semantics, full SQLite spec with DDL+connection pool, full LMDB spec with DBI layout+heed, comparison table, benchmark spec with decision thresholds, Store trait implementation signatures for both, watch notification with subscribe-before-replay race-free pattern, phased delivery.

Scheduler spec written to /ai/prompts/scheduler.md (637 lines). Decision: custom bin-spread (LeastAllocated) ~200-line Rust implementation. Crate: kube (client-side only — handles 410 Gone watch reconnect correctly). Filter pipeline: NodeReady, ResourceFit, NodeSelector, TaintToleration. Score: (remaining_cpu + remaining_memory) / 2. Binding via POST /binding API. Failure events + exponential backoff retry. kube-scheduler escape hatch documented. Top risk: pod allocation accounting on MODIFIED/terminal events — requires pod_allocations side-map keyed by UID.

6. Estimated at OOM time (60s in): 30+ stuck pods × 100 MB = ~3 GB pods + kubelet 150 MB + crio 140 MB + system ~600 MB = ~4 GB total → kernel OOM triggers.
7. Kernel OOM-killer picked e2e.test as victim because it had the highest RSS among MOVABLE processes at that moment (e2e.test cgroup ~105 MB).

So mayor-5v9gl IS the primary root cause. mayor-kkbe6 (this bead) was mis-framed as an independent OOM issue when it's actually the DOWNSTREAM SYMPTOM of pull-QPS-exceeded → cgroup pileup.

Scout v2 aa82864c86ab81711 ROOT-CAUSED with grep-verified evidence chain. NOT a rustls/webpki/cert-code bug — it's a host-port collision in conformance tooling.

MECHANISM: mayor-rcujn v2 scout invoked run-all.sh --reset --stack-only --vm lima-node-4 --port 6446 WITHOUT --kubelet-port. Per scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh:75, KUBELET_PORT defaults to 10250. Per lima-start.sh:96, the VM's lima-config hostPort is only patched when --kubelet-port is non-default. Result: lima-node-4's kubelet forward CONFLICTED with lima-node's (operator's healthy stack, holding 127.0.0.1:10250 since ~4h earlier via PID 56482 hostagent). Operator's stack won the bind race; lima-node-4's forward silently failed.

CONSEQUENCE: apiserver on lima-node-4 tries to exec into pods on lima-node-4, connects to 127.0.0.1:10250, but reaches lima-node's kubelet instead. That kubelet presents CN=lima-node's serving cert signed by lima-node's CA key. Because every u7s CA is minted with the SAME hardcoded Subject CN=u7s-ca (crates/apiserver/src/tls.rs:179), lima-node-4 apiserver's rustls WebPkiServerVerifier finds a name-matching trust anchor in its root store and attempts cryptographic verification. But the leaf was signed by a DIFFERENT stack's CA private key — legitimate BadSignature. Rustls is behaving correctly.

VERIFIED (mayor grep-checked scout's claims):
1. tls.rs:179 + tls.rs:192 both hardcode 'u7s-ca' as Subject CN. Confirmed.
2. lima-start.sh:75/94-96 gate hostPort patching on --kubelet-port being non-default. Confirmed.
3. lsof -n -i :10250 shows lima-node's hostagent PID 56482 holding the port. Confirmed live.

SCOUT EVIDENCE:
- Phase 1 cert-diff: affected/healthy CA + leaf certs structurally identical. openssl verify -x509_strict passes on affected pair. NO structural anomaly to blame.
- Phase 2 minimal rustls reproducer (rustls 0.23 + aws-lc-rs, mirrors build_kubelet_tls_config exactly): affected cert pair VERIFIES OK in isolation. Contradicts live failure -> forces the pivot.
- Live: openssl s_client -connect 127.0.0.1:10250 returned CN=lima-node cert with serial af:a1:c6:a3:10:33:a1:3f = byte-identical to temp/u7s/kubelet-serving.crt. Apiserver was talking to wrong VM entirely.

NOT A u7s CODE BUG (in tls.rs/proxy.rs/rustls consumers). Rustls is validating exactly correctly. The bug is in conformance tooling that lets two concurrently-running stacks silently collide on host port 10250.

FIX RECOMMENDATIONS (from scout, all valid):
1. HIGH: file bead to make run-all.sh/lima-start.sh auto-allocate or hard-fail on port collision instead of silently succeeding. Prevents recurrence.
2. MEDIUM: give each stack's CA a unique Subject CN so future misroute surfaces as legible UnknownIssuer instead of opaque BadSignature. Diagnostic improvement.
3. LOW: regression test in conformance tooling (verify effective host-port binding matches intended VM). NOT in tls.rs/proxy.rs.

Verdict: DEFER. Estimated reachable RSS floor if pursued: ~50-90MB (central ~65-70MB), a 3-4x reduction from the observed 234MB peak -- not the aspirational 10x/~25MB target. 25MB is not credible without dropping cadvisor-equivalent stats entirely (breaks metrics-server/kubectl top) and/or weakening PLEG responsiveness (risks Conformance pod-transition-latency assertions).

Top-3 highest-leverage subsystems:
1. cadvisor (embedded manager) -- REPLACE. Even kubelet's "CRI stats" path still calls cadvisor for pod-level cpu/mem/network aggregates, filesystem info, and MachineInfo(); a persistent always-on manager (fsnotify watches, 10-15s housekeeping, 2min history cache) serves what is fundamentally an on-demand need (metrics-server scrapes every 15-60s). Largest single subsystem, ~40-70MB estimated.
2. container manager policy managers (cpuManager/memoryManager/topologyManager/deviceManager/draManager) -- SHRINK. All constructed unconditionally even with policy=none; no evidence u7s's workload uses CPU pinning/NUMA/GPU/DRA. Cgroup/QoS enforcement itself is spec-mandated KEEP; only the pluggable-policy scaffolding is droppable. ~10-20MB estimated.
3. client-go informers (node/service listers) -- SHRINK. Service informer caches ALL cluster Services (O(cluster), not O(node)); u7s apiserver already serves cheap narrow watches server-side. ~5-15MB estimated.

Why DEFER not GO-WITH-SCOPE-LIMITS: kubelet's memory posture was rated "watch" (not "needs-work") in mayor-ja8ll's audit -- 234MB in an 8GiB VM with 1.6GB+ free throughout, did not block or slow the 446/446-green Conformance run. Reimplementation requires rewriting across two hard external protocol boundaries (CRI, CNI) for an estimated 4-6 weeks of effort to reclaim ~150-180MB on a component that isn't currently a bottleneck. Memory ranks below correctness/Conformance in the stated priority hierarchy; no current pressure signal justifies the investment now.
